rules.tip: Buy or pick what gets the deck through the next fights. Early damage, low-cost Block and draw can beat a slower engine piece. Compare cards like Pommel Strike, Shrug It Off, Iron Wave and Flame Barrier against the actual gap.

Take a payoff only when its setup is already repeatable. Check energy, hand flow and how often the payoff will be drawn with its enablers. Skip redundant attacks or speculative payoffs in a functioning deck.
Evaluate Feed as a finisher. If it can safely land the killing blow, count the maximum HP gain. Take the confirmed kill now if waiting would expose you to a dangerous extra turn.
An exhaust package needs dependable exhaust and a payoff. Check which card would be removed, how much Block or draw it produces now, and whether the deck still has a finisher after thinning.

Check the actual trigger density of attack payoffs. Hellraiser needs Strike cards, while a card rewarding several attacks needs enough cheap attacks in one turn. Measure self-damage and whether the added draw or energy can be used now.

Before the engine is reliable, stabilize with affordable damage and defense, and favor a route with manageable fights and available recovery. Once damage scales, reward draw and hand consistency over a second unrelated damage engine.

This deck already has multiple ways to produce Shivs. Leading Strike supplies Shivs but its own damage is separate. A damage-only enchantment on a generator changes only the generator's own attack. Compare the actual preview and HP cost. Accuracy adds damage to the Shivs themselves, Sharp Edge upgrades newly made Shivs, and Fan of Knives gives them area damage. Compare adding more generators against the actual need for those payoffs, draw, and defense.

Serpent Form rewards a high number of cheap plays. Activate it before expendable Shivs when the threat budget allows it. Keep room for generated Shivs and allow for the Form's random targeting in multi-enemy fights.

With Corrosive Wave, compare applying it before your main draw sequence. Draw, energy and discard cycling can improve both Poison and access to defense. Accelerant is valuable once there is meaningful Poison to trigger.

Evaluate Adrenaline and Calculated Gamble as consistency tools. An offered Serpent Form or Corrosive Wave can open an engine, and support picks depend on how reliably the deck can activate it and survive setup.
Plan what will be lost before using a full-hand discard. Spend any important defense first if the replacement hand cannot be trusted, and keep enough room to draw or generate cards.

Use efficient attacks, area damage or Block to stabilize first. Focused Strike, Lightning Rod and Boost Away are examples to compare against the deck's immediate gaps. Check Spinner's setup time before using it to cover an urgent fight.

For orbs, plan channel and evoke order before replacing an orb. Keep Frost when you need defense. With Dark, estimate the time needed to grow and evoke the payoff. With focused Lightning effects, target the enemy you need to remove.
A cheap-card loop needs more than its payoff. Confirm the discard targets for Hologram or All for One, energy and draw to replay them, and immediate defense when the loop is incomplete.
Check actual Status density and timing before taking Status payoffs. Overclock can fix a draw problem, and Compact or Iteration become stronger only when their visible triggers occur often enough.
Set up a copied Power only when the next Power and its energy cost are available. Compare a slow scaling Power with what the current turn needs to prevent damage.

Start with damage and defense you can use immediately. Build a dependable mix of Star generation, draw, manageable spenders and a finisher. A strong Star spender is less valuable when the deck cannot fund it regularly.
Track energy and Stars separately. Count Stars already banked, Stars gained this turn and what block may require. Compare an efficient kill now with saving Stars for a better payoff next turn.
Use Glow or other funded draw and generation to make spenders consistent. Hidden Cache has a delayed component. Count only the resources available before the chosen attack or defensive play.
Before Radiate, compare gaining more Stars this turn with playing it now. Before a multi-hit finisher, check Vulnerable and lethal by target, including how many resources will remain for defense.

When reliable defense already buys time, repeated Forge can provide the finisher. Treat card-creation and expensive-card branches as options when Arsenal or Void Form and their support actually exist. Check Void Form's immediate turn-ending effect.

Stabilize with efficient defense and enough immediate value before elites. Keep the deck compact. Use Souls, dependable draw and energy to reach a finisher rather than adding several slow damage payoffs.

Keep the Soul engine accessible. Draw and Block can fit together through Grave Warden. Check whether the next Soul, reusable energy card or finisher is actually accessible this turn before expecting a repeatable loop.

Treat Doom as delayed damage. Unless a live action resolves the kill immediately, defend against the enemy's action before Doom settles. Apply Doom first when the order unlocks an immediate defensive payoff such as Death's Door.

Use efficient Ethereal cards to bridge early fights and count the loss of an unplayed Ethereal card at end of turn. Only add narrow Ethereal payoffs once the deck will trigger them. Check the order of Sculpting Strike and Veilpiercer.
Osty can bridge defense and damage if you can preserve or rebuild its HP. Compare Summon with immediate Block. Check whether Osty already attacked before relying on Flatten's discounted cost.
Once Hang is a real finisher, improve access to it through draw and a compact deck. Repeat it on the same priority target and check Intangible or other visible defenses before assuming a kill.

Build only after the offers support it. Take enough immediate damage and defense to leave Act 1 safely. If rewards justify early normal fights, keep a path to a rest or an elite bypass if the deck comes together slowly.
With Quick Shot, plan how to establish Impaled and then use the conditional follow-up. Compare Ki Hop or Wah Hammer with an independent card before buying more Impaled payoffs.

Treat loose Arrows, Impaled targets and the Shoot card's location as separate state. When useful, take the Impaled payoff first, then dislodge with Wrest. Arrow Stab recovers from discard, while Locked In retrieves from the draw pile.

Consider a compact draw and retrieval loop around a Shot that the current deck can find repeatedly. Divine Shot and an upgraded Melodic Shot were possible payoffs in this run. Avoid adding default Vulnerable or high-cost cards that do not solve a fight or maintain the loop.
Check hand space and exact Melody triggers before playing Motif or Lullaby. Use Encore only after planning around its play limit. Distinguish shuffling a card to the top from having an Innate card.
